PV candidate survey: diatomic molecules and ions

Polyatomic rows are shown. They are screening estimates from rotational constants and bF (mostly the parent diatomic's bF, with a 50% floor), and their ground state is not checked unless the Gate column says otherwise. The ranked heff table and dual-isotope pairs follow the main table.

We look for diatomic molecules and singly charged ions whose ground state suits nuclear-spin-dependent parity-violation (NSD-PV) measurements, where a rotational interval 2B(N+1) nearly matches the hyperfine interval hf = (I+½)|bF|. Each row is one isotopologue. By default, the table shows only rows whose ground state is surely or probably 2Σ; tick the other 2Σ? boxes to see the rest. δ0 is the zero-field gap between opposite-parity levels of equal F in N = 0 and N = 1. δmin is the smallest such gap over N ≤ 7 (N ≤ 9 for InBr+, whose matching pair is 8↔9). On rows with an effective-Hamiltonian (heff) model, both are the strong pair (the nearest pair with |O|/I > 0.02, the only pairs useful for NSD-PV) of the full model (c, γ, eQq0 and, where computed, the ligand spin); on the other rows they come from the survey's simpler levels: exact levels where c or γ is known (or S ≥ 1), and 2B(N+1) − hf otherwise. The Gap source column says which. Each ± is the 1σ uncertainty from B and bF, plus γ on heff rows (see Methods). The N pair boxes (2↔3 means N = 2 and N = 3) restrict δmin and Bc to those pairs. A crossing's pair is the N ↔ N+1 block that carries its PV matrix element ⟨a|O|b⟩, not the N labels of its two levels: a level that mixes N = 0 and 2, or carries a few percent of another N, takes its coupling from the pair it borrows it from. A crossing is labelled with, and counts under, every pair that carries at least 20% of |⟨a|O|b⟩| (both, for example "0↔1, 1↔2"). Use the Plot selector above the graph to switch between 2B vs (I+½)|bF| and the |WA| views (|δmin|, |bF|/B, hf/2B, |δ0|, Bc), or pick any two numeric columns with X column and Y column (a log axis plots the magnitude). "As-if-Σ" rows have an unknown ground state, so their constants assume the unpaired electron occupies a σ orbital. The DFT-state columns give the state our DFT found and the energies (cm⁻¹) of the other states, relative to it; they are not a ground-state assignment. Ground states in grey italics with ? are estimated by analogy with another molecule, not taken from a source on this one.

Columns
The table shows only the isotopologues selected in the plot.
Ranked polyatomics (ticket 05: exact heff Zeeman scans, 0-500 mT, against the parent diatomic): rows with a strong crossing (|O|/I ≥ 0.2) below 200 mT first, by WA|O|/I of the lowest one. Parent columns are the production diatomic's numbers.
Dual-carrier-isotope pairs (ticket 05): two isotopologues of different carrier isotopes on one geometry and one WA, each scanned; ratio = (|O|/I)a / (|O|/I)b at their lowest strong crossings; robust = every bF ± 1σ variant of both keeps a strong crossing ≤ 200 mT.

Methods

Constants. Each B and bF carries its source: measured; scaled from a measured or calculated isotopologue of the same molecule; calculated in the literature; our CC; our DFT; or our estimate. Scaling between isotopologues (reduced mass for B, nuclear g-factor for bF) is as accurate as the parent value, so a value scaled from a calculation counts as a calculation. Our estimates either rescale another molecule of the same charge (approximate) or start from atomic radii or the free-ion contact interaction (zero order, crude). Where several values exist, we use the most direct: measured first, estimated last.

DFT. We use ORCA 6.1.1 with all-electron scalar-relativistic Hamiltonians. An unrestricted Kohn–Sham scan of the bond length gives re and Be; at re, an X2C calculation (decontracted x2c-TZVPall-s basis, finite nucleus, picture-change corrected) gives bF and c. A DKH2 g-tensor calculation gives Δg⊥, and hence γ = −2BΔg⊥ (Curl relation). We chose the functional for each class of molecule (B3LYP, PBE0 with 40% exact exchange, or BP86) by benchmarking against measured molecules. The class's RMS error sets the bF uncertainty (25% for molecules outside every benchmarked class), and the gaps use at least 20%. The x2c basis sets stop at Rn, so for Ra, Ac and Th we use Dyall's uncontracted all-electron v3z basis.

Coupled cluster. For InF+, we compute bF and c with relativistic coupled cluster (four-component Dirac–Coulomb CCSD(T) in DIRAC 26.1, uncontracted Dyall v3z basis, 47 electrons correlated). Finite-field energy differences give A∥ and A⊥, so that c = A∥ − A⊥ and bF = A∥ − 2c/3. The same calculation on 113Cd+, which is isoelectronic with In2+ and has a measured 5s hyperfine constant, falls 3% short, so we scale A∥ by the measured/CC ratio. We then apply the v = 0 vibrational average (−0.5%). B0 uses the calculated bond length of Borschevsky et al. (1.91 Å, Phys. Rev. A 86, 050501(R) (2012)) with αe from our CCSD(T) scan (first-order Dunham, Be − αe/2). To test the recipe on a measured molecule, we applied it to ZnCl with Cu as the reference atom. It misses the measured A∥ by 3%, and we take that as the bF uncertainty. For GaCl+ and GaBr+, a first pass used the smaller v2z basis with c from our DFT. At that level CC underestimates the measured A∥ of the isoelectronic neutrals ZnCl and ZnBr by 9–10% (our DFT by 3%), so each cation would be scaled by the measured/CC ratio of its Zn-halide partner; those first-pass values are not in the table. The table carries the final ones: the same basis at the CC bond length with c from CC, scaled by the midpoint of two anchors (the measured Zn halide and the Cu atom) and averaged over v = 0. Where a CC value exists, the gaps use it instead of DFT, and the table lists both.

Estimates. Without a measured or calculated value, we estimate the bond length from related molecules of the same charge, scaled by covalent radii (Pyykkö–Atsumi), or from atomic radii alone when no related molecule is known. For bF, we scale the Fermi contact interaction of a related molecule, or of the free ion, to the target nucleus. Leave-one-out tests on molecules with known values set the uncertainties, and the gaps use at least 50% for bF. Estimates are placeholders until a measurement or calculation exists.

Anapole constant (WA). The table reports WA (Hz) on the carrier nucleus without forming a composite score: (1) four-component relativistic calculations from the literature, plus raw two-component ZORA values from Isaev & Berger (J. Mol. Spectrosc. 300, 26 (2014), 25% uncertainty) where no four-component value exists—their hyperfine-rescaled ZORA values are omitted because dσ dipolar mixing and p1/2 spin–orbit coupling break single-s–p proportionality; (2) our four-component Dirac–Coulomb CCSD(T) finite-field calculations in DIRAC 26.1 (InF+, CuAl+, HfS+); (3) isotopologue scaling via the relativistic nuclear-size factor R(A, Z); and (4) for remaining 2Σ molecules, isovalent Z2 R(A, Z) column scaling within core-contraction sub-blocks (~21% LOO RMS) and same-carrier ligand-group transfer (~27% LOO RMS), followed by Kozlov's semiempirical hyperfine relation from bF and c (Sov. Phys. JETP 62, 1114 (1985), median calibration 0.86, ~32% LOO RMS), gated off heavy 6p1/2 carriers (Z ≥ 81) and transition-metal bonds to second-row or heavier atoms.

Uncertainties. δ0 and δmin follow one rule, to first order in B and bF: σ² = [2(N+1)σB]² + [(hf/|bF|)σbF]². We use a value's stated uncertainty where it has one. Without one, a measured value, or one scaled from a measured isotopologue, counts as exact, and a gap with no uncertainty at all shows no ±; any other value takes 5% on B and 20% on bF. The floors above still apply to bF from our DFT and from estimates. σ leaves out c, γ and model error. When σ(δmin) exceeds 2B, the N of closest approach is itself unknown, so the ± is only a scale.

Polyatomic rows (shown with the polyatomic box; data/polyatomic_table.csv from data/shards/polyatomic-site.csv, survey/polyatomic.py). Analogues of the diatomic carriers with a polyatomic ligand. Geometries follow the literature audit's rule (bond lengths from the fluoride plus a measured ionic offset, or literature lengths), except that HgOH uses a literature DFT geometry (bent), and InOH+ (bent) and the Lu amide and boryl cations (LuNH2+, LuBH2+ and their D forms) our DFT minimum. Linear and C3v molecules (K = 0 levels only: |K| = 1 pairs anticross at zero field) use the diatomic formula δN = 2B(N+1) − (I+½)|bF|. Asymmetric tops use the rigid-rotor interval from A, B and C instead: N0N → (N+1)0,N+1 for the component of n on a, (N+1)1,N+1 on b (bent ML2: 000 ↔ 111 at A + C), (N+1)1,N on c, where n points from the metal to the bonded atom. bF is measured where known (171,173YbOH, 87SrCCH; their OD and CCD partners take the same value); for the species of our ground-state check, our coupled cluster calibrated on measured anchors with its own error, else our DFT scaled by that calibration (20% floor, 40% where the DFT is spin-contaminated); otherwise the parent diatomic's (estimated, 50% floor), where a parent our coupled cluster recalibrated (HgF, 20360 ± 916 MHz) enters with that value. B and A, B, C take 5%. P1GHz is the summed chance over N that |δN| ≤ 1 GHz. These rows have no level plots, and the 2Σ? and ground-state filters skip them; the Gate column gives the ground-state check (EOM-CCSD verdict and gap to the lowest competing state; gaps below 0.4 eV are labelled uncertain; methyl rows take the gate of their OH, NH or CH stand-in). With the polyatomic box ticked, two tables follow the main table: the ranked polyatomics from exact heff Zeeman scans against their parent diatomic, and the dual-carrier-isotope pairs, each with its provenance and risk flags (from the ticket-05 notes; the Ez + B column with methyl spins on from the C3v rerun).

Levels and crossings. For 2Σ molecules with enough known constants, we diagonalize the effective Hamiltonian (case (b) basis |N G F MF⟩, with γ, bF, c and eQq) in magnetic fields up to 200 mT. The level plots and crossings show only same-MF, opposite-parity pairs whose PV matrix element |⟨a|n·(I×S)|b⟩|/I exceeds 0.02. The basis stops at N = 11 (13 for InBr+), so the pairs shown sit well inside it; crossings that move by more than 1 G at N = 13 (15) are left out of Bc. For each row the page lists, among the crossings under the ticked N pairs, the X with the smallest max(Bc, B0)/(|O|/I) below a cut (defaults X = 3, cut = 50 mT, field floor B0 = 5 mT; set B0 = 0 for no floor), then one more: the largest |O|/I between the cut and 100 mT, else between 100 and 200 mT. The first listed is the headline crossing Bc. At Bc, |WA|·|O|/I is the weak matrix element up to κA and I, and max(Bc, B0)/(|WA|·|O|/I) and max(Bc, B0)/(|O|/I) are figures of merit to minimize; the 1σ plot bars carry the WA uncertainty only. The detail panel plots every crossing of the row below 200 mT, |O|/I against field, by N pair.
